papers.name: Paper 1 Explorations in creative reading and writing

topics.name: Section A Reading: 20th- or 21st-century literary prose fiction
points: Reading unseen literary fiction: identifying and interpreting themes, ideas and information
Question 1: identify explicit information from a given part of the extract (AO1, 4 marks; multiple-choice from summer 2026)
Question 2: analyse the writer's language: words, phrases, language features and techniques, sentence forms (AO2, 8 marks)
Question 3: analyse how the writer structures the whole text, e.g. shifts in focus, to create an effect (AO2, 8 marks)
Question 4: critically evaluate a statement about part of the extract, agreeing and/or disagreeing, with textual references (AO4, 20 marks)
Drawing inferences and justifying them with evidence from the text
Using accurate linguistic and literary terminology to explain effects

topics.name: Section B Writing: descriptive or narrative writing
points: Question 5: descriptive writing, which may use a visual image as a prompt (AO5, AO6, 40 marks)
Question 5: narrative writing, e.g. writing the opening of a story
Content and organisation: matching tone, style and register to audience and purpose (AO5, 24 marks)
Organising writing: structural and grammatical features, paragraphs and coherence
Using language imaginatively and creatively; creating emotional impact; consistent point of view
Technical accuracy: vocabulary, sentence structures, spelling and punctuation, Standard English (AO6, 16 marks)

topics.name: Section A Reading: one non-fiction and one literary non-fiction text (19th century and 20th or 21st century)
points: Reading 19th-, 20th- and 21st-century non-fiction and literary non-fiction, including reviews and journalism
Question 1: identify true statements from a given part of a source (AO1, 4 marks)
Question 2: summary: select and synthesise evidence from both sources, e.g. differences (AO1, 8 marks)
Question 3: analyse how a writer uses language to achieve effects in one source (AO2, 12 marks)
Question 4: compare writers' ideas and perspectives and how they are conveyed across both sources (AO3, 16 marks)
Critical reading: identifying bias and misuse of evidence; supported and unsupported claims
Reading in context and recognising that texts can be read in different valid ways

topics.name: Section B Writing: writing to present a viewpoint
points: Question 5: writing to present a viewpoint for a specified audience, purpose and form, e.g. an article, letter or speech (40 marks)
Writing to argue, persuade, explain and inform: selecting, organising and emphasising facts, ideas and key points
Rhetorical devices, e.g. rhetorical questions, antithesis and parenthesis
Citing evidence and quotation effectively to support views
Content and organisation: tone, style and register for audience and purpose (AO5, 24 marks)
Technical accuracy: vocabulary, sentence structures, spelling and punctuation (AO6, 16 marks)

topics.name: Spoken Language endorsement (non-exam assessment)
points: Selecting and organising information and ideas for a prepared formal presentation, agreed in advance with the teacher
Planning for different purposes and audiences; presentation formats (talk, speech, debate or dialogue)
Giving the presentation in a formal setting (up to about ten minutes)
Listening and responding appropriately to questions and feedback
Using spoken Standard English
Pass, Merit and Distinction criteria; graded separately and not part of the 9 to 1 grade
